rows.description: Complex problems get reduced to a hated group or figure who is to blame. Having a target eases helplessness, and the person starts to see members of that group only as a category.
graph_context: next stage: Echo chamber and dehumanising talk
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Stage 4: Echo chamber and dehumanising talk [Actor]
rows.description: The person joins forums where jokes, slurs and contempt are normal and disagreement is treated as betrayal. Mocking others becomes a way to bond, and empathy shrinks.
graph_context: previous stage: A villain is named
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: contempt, empathy

rows.subtype: Stage 4: Echo chamber and dehumanising talk [Observer]
rows.description: A friend notices someone who was funny and gentle now speaks in absolutes, sneers at whole groups and stays online at night. Signs include repeated scapegoating and loss of interest in anything else.
graph_context: previous stage: A villain is named
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, interest

rows.description: A teacher or older sibling hears a scapegoating rant and asks what the person is really afraid of. Taking the underlying fear seriously, while calmly disagreeing with the hatred, keeps the conversation open.
graph_context: next stage: Echo chamber and dehumanising talk
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, calm

rows.description: Anger leaks into family, work and friendships, and the person loses sleep, trust and sometimes a job. Some feel the exhaustion and emptiness of constant rage, which can be the crack that lets doubt in.
graph_context: next stage: A human contact breaks the frame
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: anger, doubt, tiredness, trust

rows.subtype: Stage 6: A human contact breaks the frame [Response]
rows.description: A calm conversation, a kind act from someone of the hated group or a family member who still listens shows the category has people in it. Curiosity, not debate victories, is what moves a person.
graph_context: previous stage: Real-life costs
next stage: Redirecting the anger
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: curiosity, calm

rows.description: The person steps back from feeds, sleeps, sees a counsellor if needed and channels the grievance into concrete, lawful work such as local action or learning. Anger about injustice is valid, and hatred of people is what needs to be dropped.
graph_context: previous stage: A human contact breaks the frame
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: grief, anger

rows.description: A teen learns that real institutions do not demand secrecy, instant payment or gift cards. A rule to pause and check through an official number before acting works against nearly every scam.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: detachment

rows.description: A stranger or spoof call, message or job offer arrives at a moment of need, such as a bill, loneliness or ambition. The approach is friendly or urgent and appears to come from a bank, courier, officer or admirer.
graph_context: next stage: Trust building
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, anger, loneliness

rows.description: The victim gets warmth, small proofs and plausible details, and starts to feel special or safe. Smart, careful people fall for scams because the manipulator works on emotion, not intelligence.
graph_context: previous stage: The approach
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: affection, trust
